choices.source_assertion_strength: Authors explicitly claim ease of methodological extension; implementation changes do not themselves negate ease; adaptation effort not independently measured.

claim_evidence.paraphrase: Platform maintainer, white-box access, general corpus with sufficient task-related examples; no trigger input test samples. Core scope is classification.

PICCOLO and DBS previously evaluated one dynamic syntax attack; CLIBE authors argue detection depends on reference-subset choice, unlike a dependable trigger-agnostic solution. Not proof nobody ever studied dynamic attacks.
Landscape visualization is a 2D parameter subspace; theory uses simplified data and a two-layer TextCNN. Source support is not a general theorem for arbitrary Transformer detectors.
Confidence-filtered reference samples; a small subset forms probe, remaining samples evaluate generalization; overfitting can occur even with a small perturbation budget.

Distribution concentration rather than merely high mean is linked to resistance against tested adaptive confidence changes; alternative metric can score better on some ordinary RoBERTa configurations.
24 source-agnostic configurations, each row 40 backdoor and 40 benign models; headline is average, not per-configuration floor.

AG-News BERT rows; each row evaluates 48 backdoor models for TPR and 40 benign models for FPR; source-specific syntax TPR .583 FPR .075 F1 .709 AUC .758, PICCOLO AUC .781. Caption mentions RoBERTa but rows and body do not supply RoBERTa measurements.
CLIBE fixed threshold; comparator thresholds optimized for F1 subject to FPR no more than .10.

Three evaluated adaptive strategies do not effectively evade CLIBE. Their tested populations differ; the bounded conclusion is not zero misses, universal robustness, or inheritance of the two-architecture benchmark.
